t: Edit video and podcasts by editing the transcript
note: Still the fastest path from raw recording to publishable cut. Overkill for pure audio.

t: Free short-form video editor with auto-captions
note: Free, ubiquitous, and the template library is the real product.

t: Turns long videos into ranked short clips
note: Virality scoring is directionally useful, not gospel. Always re-cut the hook.

t: Voice cloning, dubbing and text-to-speech
note: Best-in-class quality. Get written consent before cloning any voice.

t: Studio-quality remote recording for video podcasts
note: Local recording means a dropped call no longer ruins the episode.

t: Backlink and keyword research for content teams
note: The index is the moat. Expensive, and worth it above ~50 pages of content.

t: All-in-one SEO, PPC and content marketing suite
note: Broader than Ahrefs, shallower per module.

t: On-page content scoring against live SERP data
note: Useful guardrail. Writing to the score alone produces forgettable pages.

t: Brand-voice AI writing for marketing teams
note: Value is the brand-voice layer and workflow, not raw generation.

t: Long-context assistant for research, drafting and code
note: Strongest long-document reasoning in the category.

t: General assistant with browsing, images and code
note: Widest plugin and integration surface of any assistant.

t: Cited answer engine for fast research
note: Citations make it checkable. Still verify the primary source.

t: High-fidelity AI image generation
note: Aesthetic ceiling is the highest; control is the lowest.

t: Design, video and brand kit for non-designers
note: Brand kits plus scheduling make it a genuine content system, not just an editor.

t: Collaborative interface and brand design
note: Overkill for thumbnails; essential once a brand system exists.

t: Instant background removal and product shots
note: Best-in-class cutouts at e-commerce volume.

t: A/B test YouTube thumbnails before publishing
note: CTR lift is real but small-sample results mislead. Run 5,000+ impressions.

t: YouTube optimisation, bulk edits and A/B tests
note: The bulk-edit tools pay for themselves on a 200-video library.

t: YouTube keyword scores and competitor tracking
note: Scores are a heuristic. Use the competitor tracking, ignore the gamification.

t: Public channel statistics and growth history
note: Its earnings estimates are famously wide. Use our calculators instead.

t: Simple multi-platform scheduling
note: Cheapest credible scheduler for a solo operator.

t: Visual planner for Instagram and TikTok
note: Grid preview still the best in class for visual brands.

t: Enterprise social management and approvals
note: Bought for compliance and approvals, not for delight.

t: Scheduling plus competitor analytics on one plan
note: Best value analytics stack under $20/month.

t: Newsletter platform with built-in ad network
note: The ad network and boosts marketplace are why publishers switch.

t: Creator-first email marketing and automation
note: Formerly ConvertKit. Visual automations are the strong point.

t: Publishing plus paid subscriptions, zero setup
note: 10% of revenue forever. Cheap at the start, expensive at scale.

t: Open-source publishing with memberships
note: Own your list and your CSS. Self-host if you can operate it.

t: Recurring memberships for creators
note: Discovery is weak; it is a billing layer, not an audience.

t: One-off tips and simple memberships
note: Lowest-friction donation widget that works on a static site.

t: Tips, shop and commissions with 0% platform fee
note: 0% on donations is genuinely 0%. The embeddable widget is one script tag.

t: No-code checkout URLs for any static site
note: The correct answer for selling from a static site.

t: Sell digital products with zero infrastructure
note: Flat 10% fee. Fine for a first product, painful at volume.

t: Merchant of record for digital goods
note: Handles global VAT for you — the real reason to pay the premium.

t: Live meeting transcription and summaries
note: Accuracy dips hard on accented speech and crosstalk.

t: Open-source speech-to-text you can self-host
note: Free, offline, and better than most paid services.

t: Human-verified transcription and captions
note: Pay for humans when the transcript is legally or editorially load-bearing.

t: Connect the tools in your content pipeline
note: Cost scales with task volume faster than teams expect.

t: Visual automation with granular control
note: Cheaper than Zapier at volume; steeper learning curve.

t: Self-hostable workflow automation
note: Self-host and the per-task pricing problem disappears entirely.

t: Content calendar, brief library and wiki
note: Becomes the editorial system of record for most small teams.

t: Structured content pipelines and asset databases
note: The right home for a 500-row content calendar.

t: Frame-accurate video review and approvals
note: Kills the 'which cut is this' email thread permanently.

t: Professional editing and colour, free tier
note: The free tier is a genuinely professional NLE. No subscription, ever.

t: Industry-standard video editing
note: Ubiquitous in agencies, which is the main reason to learn it.

t: Generative video and AI editing tools
note: Best for b-roll and impossible shots, not full narrative edits.

t: Browser video editing with auto-subtitles
note: Fast for captions and resizing; weak for anything complex.

t: Animated captions and b-roll for short clips
note: Caption styling is its whole value. Judge it on that alone.

t: Free high-resolution stock photography
note: Free, but everyone uses the same 200 photos. Shoot your own where it matters.

t: Free stock photos and video clips
note: Video library is the differentiator over Unsplash.

t: Cleared music and SFX for monetised video
note: Clearance is the product. A single claim costs more than a year's subscription.

t: Music, SFX and footage on one licence
note: Broader licence than Epidemic; smaller catalogue depth.

t: AI avatars and video translation
note: Translation with lip-sync is the killer feature; avatars still read synthetic.

t: Human-reviewed AI dubbing for publishers
note: Enterprise-priced. Justified only when a back catalogue is being localised.

t: Free web and app analytics
note: Free and universally supported. The reporting UI is its own punishment.

t: Privacy-first, cookie-free web analytics
note: No cookie banner needed. One script, 1KB, and the numbers are legible.

t: Simple privacy-focused analytics
note: Same pitch as Plausible. Pick on price and hosting region.

t: Ad mediation and layout testing for publishers
note: Lifts RPM over raw AdSense but can wreck Core Web Vitals if left unattended.

t: Premium ad management for content sites
note: Higher RPM than AdSense once you clear the sessions threshold. The approval bar is the moat.

t: Ad management for large content publishers
note: Formerly AdThrive. For sites already doing serious pageview volume.

t: Search performance and indexing diagnostics
note: Free first-party search data. Nothing else replaces it.

t: Desktop crawler for technical SEO audits
note: 500 URLs free. The paid licence is the cheapest line in an SEO budget.

t: Content optimisation for editorial teams
note: Cleaner recommendations than Surfer; priced for teams, not solos.

t: Business video hosting with lead capture
note: Turnstile email gates on video are the reason to pay over YouTube.

t: Podcast hosting with private feeds and analytics
note: Unlimited shows on one plan — unusual and useful for networks.

t: Beginner-friendly podcast hosting
note: The onboarding is the product. Outgrow it around 10K downloads.

t: Automatic audio levelling and loudness targets
note: Two hours free every month, and it fixes the one thing listeners notice.
